findings.summary: The DER admission bounds (len==0, len>4096 before copy) are implemented correctly but not causally evidenced by a test.
findings.detail: empty-DER and oversize-DER copy `base`, so `expected` stays SHA256(base DER) while the DER changes. A false result is therefore already forced by `hashBytes(der) != expected` (line 30), even without the line-15 DER bounds. Only the record bound has a measured 0-allocation pre-copy proof (AllocsPerRun on over.raw, test line 329). If someone deleted `len(publicSPKIDER) > 4096` from line 15, every current test would still pass; the only effect would be a bounded 4097-byte copy plus hash before rejection.
findings.suggestedLaterFix: In a later Root-granted test card, add an oversize DER row whose expected hash and signer are rebound to SHA256(hugeDER), plus an AllocsPerRun==0 measurement on it. This is not required for this narrow code card.

findings.summary: Several helper branches are defense in depth; because the helper returns only a bool, the tests can't attribute a rejection to them.
findings.detail: p02Schema24 already fixes signatureHex to exactly 128 lowercase hex (p02Pattern 5), so signature-bytes-63/65 are rejected by the schema before `len(sig) != 64`; the test label 'codec/signature-encoding' says so honestly. The schema also fixes signer.keySPKISHA256 to 64 lowercase nonzero hex, so the uppercase/invalid/short/long/empty expected-hash rows also fail the signer equality. Go's ParsePKIXPublicKey already enforces a 32-byte Ed25519 key, no parameters, minimal DER and no trailing data, so `len(key) != 32` and the MarshalPKIX roundtrip mismatch are probably unreachable with stdlib inputs. I did not execute this; it is manual reasoning. The DER rows do pin their earlier preconditions (decode, schema and hash all hold), so their rejection must come from the parse, type or roundtrip layer. The wrong-algorithm row reaches the concrete-type assertion (X25519 OID). None of this is a defect.

findings.summary: The call exemption is keyed by call.Pos() alone, not by (position, resolved callee).
findings.detail: This is safe today. A position is registered only when one of the three exact objects is the direct call.Fun in the H12 file and the H12 helper. Any other reference to those objects fails h12ScopedCryptoUses before the call walk runs. Another CallExpr could share that start position only if it called the result of the allowed call, and Verify returns bool while ParsePKIX/MarshalPKIX return two values, so neither result can be called. This is a hardening note if a future grant ever allows an object that returns a callable.

findings.summary: The public-refusal assertion is one unconditional call after the table. It shows that no wiring exists; it is not a causal property of the re-signed-other-policy row.
findings.detail: This matches the contract: there is no caller, port or factory, and the static check confirms that no other production file names the helper. The ReadHistory, null and unregistered public refusals stay covered by the existing unchanged tests, which Root's phase 4 ran and passed (Root fact). The new files don't assert them again.

findings.summary: File identity is the bare unadjusted FileSet name, and owner identity is a package-scope, receiverless FuncDecl name. A dot-import spelling has no fixture.
findings.detail: The real-closure control at line 737 runs sourceEffects on the actual sources and must pass. The real Verify/ParsePKIX/Marshal references can only pass if the bare filename matches, so that control is the evidence that the name binding is real. A dot import of crypto/ed25519 calling Verify directly would resolve to the same object, position and direct call, so it is allowed, which is consistent with the contract and not a bypass. A dot-imported `PublicKey` assertion would be refused because it is not a SelectorExpr, which is conservative. The spelled AST check in source_gate (`id.Name == "ed25519"`) predates this change. The go/types check is the governing guard, and the new exception there requires the exact resolved object, position and allowed reference (h12ResolvedVerifyAt, line 702).

assessment.securityContract: The helper checks the bounds and expected-hash format first, then copies raw and DER, then runs the existing p02Decode(c2=false) with canonical roundtrip and the existing p02EnvelopeSchema/p02ReadEnvelope. After that it checks the exact format, purpose, signer hash and SHA256 of the full DER against the supplied expected hash (the full SPKI, not the raw 32-byte key). Then come p02Unhex to 64 bytes, ParsePKIX, the concrete ed25519.PublicKey with length 32, the MarshalPKIX roundtrip byte-equal to the full DER, the existing p02Context{envelopeValue: v}.signingInput() (fixed p02Domain||NUL||canonical {body,signer}), and finally stdlib ed25519.Verify. There are 9 `return p02SignatureTuple{}, false` exits and 1 success return naming exactly the 13 declared fields. No alternative codec, domain, JSON callback, public caller, port, factory or p02Inputs assembly was added.
assessment.inputOwnership: raw and DER are copied after the bounds check and before any parse or hash. signingInput is freshly allocated by append, sig is fresh from hex.DecodeString, and the strings come from the decoded value. The ownership test mutates the original raw and DER after the call and checks the tuple fingerprint. No concurrent or hostile isolation is claimed; the doc comment says so.
assessment.oracle: The test signs with deterministic public NewKeyFromSeed/Sign over a message built by stdlib encoding/json: the literal domain constant, then NUL, then the WHOLE body and signer RawMessages. It never calls the helper or signingInput. The math rows independently re-verify the original message and check the canonical/schema/hash/DER preconditions before checking the result. The expected 13-field tuple is rebuilt from stdlib JSON and the oracle message.
assessment.preconditions: Math rows: decode, schema, signer hash, DER hash and canonical DER all hold, and only the signed message, key or signature varies. DER rows: decode, schema and hash hold, so rejection must come from the parse, type or roundtrip layer. Depth row: the bounded parser itself must reject. Rows can't share a complete input (fingerprint uniqueness inside the table).
assessment.resolvedGuard: The new type restriction applies only to `file == h12SignatureSource`, which is the WIP01 fix. The three functions must be *types.Func, in the H12 file, owned by the H12 helper (a nested FuncLit gives no owner), and appear as the direct call.Fun. Positions are unadjusted, so //line directives are ignored. Function values, non-call references, passing as an argument, wrappers, nested literals, foreign files, aliased imports and line-directive impersonation all have compile-valid refusal fixtures. The repository AST exception requires the exact resolved Verify at that line and column in the H12 file. The own-method mimic and column+1 controls are present. No crypto Signer, PrivateKey or Sign permission was broadened: PrivateKey in the H12 file is refused, and Sign/NewKeyFromSeed appear only in the test fixture.
